meta.title: RDK Course | Lesson 09: RDK X5 Display Module

slides.title: Display Module [gradient]HDMI and DSI Verification[/gradient]
slides.lead: Build a complete HDMI evidence chain, then verify DSI independently with a shorter hardware, wiring, and visible-output sequence.

slides.title: A Lit Screen Is Only the Start
slides.lead: After this lesson, you can judge the display path at three evidence layers.

cards.title: Trusted connection
cards.body: The connector, cable, and physical monitor form a complete path.

cards.title: Readable status
cards.body: DRM and X11 both identify the connector and active mode.

cards.title: Visible result
cards.body: Color, grayscale, text, fine lines, and motion can all be judged.

slides.title: Prepare the Hardware and Set Boundaries
slides.lead: This lesson only reads display status and runs a local demo inside the isolated project.
items: Prepare the X5, HDMI monitor, HDMI cable, and stable power
Select the correct monitor input and connect cables while powered off
Enter new_project and run source env.sh
Keep ROS_DOMAIN_ID at 42 and use only ports 9100–9199
Do not modify frozen XRD assets, original systemd services, or ROS Domain 0
Keep SSH and VNC enabled; do not change networking or display boot settings

slides.title: Verify the Display in Five Steps

steps.title: 1  Check wiring
steps.sub: Confirm the connector, cable, and input source.

steps.title: 2  Load environment
steps.sub: Enter the isolated directory and Domain 42.

steps.title: 3  Read status
steps.sub: Inspect DRM and X11 connection data.

steps.title: 5  Clean up
steps.sub: Repeat the test and verify ports and services.

cards.title: HDMI
cards.body: Carries image and audio data to an external display.

cards.title: DRM
cards.body: The Linux kernel display layer reports connector detection.

cards.title: X11
cards.body: The X5 desktop stack; xrandr reports outputs and modes.

cards.title: Display mode
cards.body: Resolution and refresh rate describe the active output.

slides.title: All Three Evidence Layers Matter
slides.lead: Screen capture shows detail, camera footage proves the real setup, and logs support review.

cards.title: Camera footage
cards.body: Proves the cable is attached to the X5 and the physical HDMI monitor is active.

cards.title: Screen capture
cards.body: Clearly shows color blocks, text, fine lines, and motion tests.

cards.title: Runtime logs
cards.body: Record the connector, active mode, port, and cleanup result.

slides.title: The Desktop Shortcut Is Not a Black Box
slides.lead: The one-click entry and terminal use the same project scripts.

cards.title: 4  Capture screen
cards.note: Saves media under the project log directory.

slides.title: Read the Measured X5 Result
slides.lead: These values come from the physical board; listed capabilities are not reported as verified results.

cards.title: HDMI-1
cards.body: Both DRM and X11 report connected.
Active mode at a 59.82 Hz refresh rate.

cards.title: Candidate modes
cards.body: 1080p and 720p are also listed, but not switched in this lesson.

slides.title: Each Test Page Checks One Thing

cards.title: Color
cards.body: RGB and CMY boundaries are clear, with no obvious color cast.

cards.title: Grayscale
cards.body: Brightness levels from 0 to 100 percent remain distinguishable.

cards.title: Detail
cards.body: Small text, one-pixel lines, checkerboards, and rings remain visible.

cards.title: Motion
cards.body: Moving edges stay continuous; browser render rate is observed separately.

slides.title: Startup and Cleanup Stay Controlled
slides.lead: The verification should not leave unrelated processes or occupied project ports.

steps.body: Double-click RDK X5 HDMI Demo and watch the five-second countdown.
The launcher selects a free port from 9100–9199 and listens only on 127.0.0.1.
The browser cycles through six pages; arrow keys and Space also work.
Press Alt+F4 to close only the browser and web service started by this project.

slides.title: Pass Only When All Six Checks Succeed
slides.lead: Success means repeatable results and a clean exit, not one momentary image.
items: DRM and X11 both report HDMI-1 as connected
The active mode matches the physical monitor: 1024×600 at 59.82 Hz
Color, grayscale, text, fine lines, geometry, and motion pages are visible
Two runs from a clean state produce the same result
Project ports are released with no project Firefox or web service left behind
SSH and VNC work, and frozen XRD service states remain unchanged

cards.title: No signal
cards.body: Check the input source, power, and cable before reading DRM status.

cards.title: Shortcut fails
cards.body: Run the launch script in a terminal and read the safety checks.

cards.title: Port in use
cards.body: Keep the existing listener; the launcher selects another free port.

cards.title: Data check
cards.body: Inspect runtime.json and server.log without restoring original services.

slides.title: DSI Needs Fewer Parts, but the Power-Off Check Still Matters
slides.lead: This test uses an RDK X5, a 4.3-inch DSI display, a 40-pin ribbon cable, and stable power. HDMI is disconnected so the result remains interface-specific.
slides.alt: RDK X5, 4.3-inch DSI display, and 40-pin ribbon cable
slides.caption: Physical evidence: the board, display, and ribbon cable are visible together.

slides.title: Check the Ribbon Orientation Before Applying Power
slides.lead: Insert both ends squarely and lock the latches. Avoid reversed, angled, or live insertion. If the screen stays dark, power off before checking orientation and contact.
slides.alt: RDK X5 connected to a 4.3-inch DSI display
slides.caption: Wiring evidence: one DSI ribbon cable links the X5 and display board.

slides.title: A Visible Physical Desktop Completes the Minimum DSI Check
slides.lead: The short camera clip keeps the board, ribbon cable, and physical screen in view, so a screen capture cannot be mistaken for hardware evidence.

cards.title: Independent path
cards.body: Only the 4.3-inch DSI display is connected; the HDMI result is not reused.

cards.title: Visible output
cards.body: The physical display shows the X5 desktop and icons without a persistent black screen.

cards.title: Bounded claim
cards.body: This proves display output, not touch input, color calibration, or long-duration stability.

slides.title: HDMI and DSI Are Both Verified on the X5
slides.lead: HDMI keeps the full reproducible workflow; DSI keeps a shorter but complete hardware, wiring, and visible-output record.

cards.title: HDMI complete
cards.body: Connection, mode, image quality, repeat runs, and cleanup are evidenced.

cards.title: DSI complete
cards.body: The 4.3-inch panel is wired correctly and shows the physical desktop.

cards.title: Claims stay separate
cards.body: Different interfaces and boards continue to use independent evidence.
